content: Tetracycline is an antibiotic used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections, including acne. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication works by inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis through binding to the 30S and possibly the 50S ribosomal subunits. How to Take Tetracycline: Take this medication orally on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or two hours after meals, as directed by your doctor. It is typically taken 2 to 4 times daily. If stomach upset occurs, consult your doctor about taking it with food. Each dose should be taken with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) to reduce the risk of esophageal irritation or ulceration. Do not lie down for at least 10 minutes after taking the medication. Avoid taking tetracycline within 2 to 3 hours of consuming products containing aluminum, calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc, or bismuth subsalicylate, as these can interfere with absorption. Examples include antacids, sucralfate, vitamins/minerals, dairy products (milk, yogurt), and calcium-enriched juice. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal results, take the medication at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, mouth sores, black hairy tongue, sore throat, dizziness, headache, and rectal discomfort. If this occurs, it usually resolves after stopping the medication, but there is a risk of permanent vision loss or blindness. Tetracycline may also rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridium difficile bacteria, which can occur during or weeks to months after treatment. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or yeast infections (oral or vaginal). Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. Precautions: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to tetracycline or other related antibiotics (e.g., doxycycline, minocycline) or if you have other allergies. This medication may cause dizziness. Avoid alcohol or marijuana (cannabis), as they can worsen this effect. Do not drive or operate machinery until you are alert. Tetracycline may make you more sensitive to sunlight. This medication should not be used in children under 8 years old, as it can cause permanent tooth discoloration and other issues. Tooth discoloration has also been reported in older children and young adults. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Tetracycline can harm an unborn baby and should not be used during pregnancy. It also passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Tetracycline can interact with various medications and substances, altering their effectiveness or increasing the risk of side effects. Examples include: Antacids, calcium, magnesium, iron, and zinc-containing products, which reduce tetracycline absorption. Live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine), which may not work effectively. Alcohol and marijuana, which can increase dizziness. Moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, which may alter tetracycline metabolism. Keep a list of all medications and supplements you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Tetracycline may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. Storage and Disposal: Store tetracycline at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication, as taking outdated tetracycline can cause serious illness. Overdose: In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention. In the U.S., call 911 for severe symptoms (e.g., passing out, trouble breathing) or contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Important Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other infections unless directed by your doctor. Keep all medical and lab appointments while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose. Tetracycline is generally considered safe for breastfeeding, as per the NIH LactMed database and the American Academy of Pediatrics. However, always consult your healthcare provider for personalized advice.
